summary: Ralph Abraham was a philosopher who studied at the University of Michigan (BSE ~1952–1956, Master ~1956–1958, Promotion ~1958–1960) and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, Princeton, and UC Santa Cruz (Associate Professor 1968, Professor 1980).
Ralph Lerner is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1947–1953) under Leo Strauss (~1949–1953). He held a post at the University of Chicago around 1953.

Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College (~1906–1910). He lectured at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1913), was Professor of Indian Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and served as Director of SOAS (1922–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford (BA ~1843–1846) under Horace Hayman Wilson. He was a member of the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885) and served as Principal of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (~1861–1878).
Ralph Waldo Emerson was a philosopher who was educated at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1817–1821), later studying at Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).
Ram Chandra Dhungana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Ram Chandra Kak was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Sri Pratap College (~1909–1913) and under John Marshall (1914–1919). He served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department and Chief Secretary in Jammu and Kashmir (1919–1929).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti (~1958–1963), and served as Professor, Head of Buddhist Studies (~1966–1973), and acharya (~1973–1997) at the University of Delhi.

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1956–1959) under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as Vice Chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded Presidency University (1816), the Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828), among other institutions.

Ram Niwas Pandey is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raghunatha Shastri and Swami Dharmamegha Aranya. His posts included research assistant at Banaras Hindu University and All-India Kashiraj Trust, as well as teacher at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He headed the Buddhist Philosophy department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977, ~1982–1994), lectured at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1999), and was Dean at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001).

Ram Sharan Sharma was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD at SOAS (~1953–1956) under A. L. Basham. He headed Patna University's history department (1958–1973) and served as Professor and Dean of History at the University of Delhi (1973–1978).

Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested as a Professor in 1889 and as Assistant Professor of Sankhya in 1914.

Rama Nath Sharma is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma, Ramaprasada Tripathi, and at the University of Rochester (PhD ~1968–1971). He was a professor at the University of Rochester (1971–1976) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1976–2012).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug (~1859–1866) and at Göttingen (PhD ~1885). He was Professor at Elphinstone College (~1868–1882) and Deccan College (~1882–1893), and Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist affiliated with the Sadhulal Research Department at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944). He later served as Head of the Veda Department at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Scottish Church College (BA ~1893–1896). He taught at the University of Calcutta (1920–1921), served as Superintendent at the Indian Museum (1921–1932), and was president of the Indian Anthropological Institute (1938–1942).

Ramaprasada Tripathi was an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he was attested as former Vice Chancellor (kulapatichara) in 1976 and further attested in 2001.
